items.title: Editing basics - watchlists
items.author: Sage Ross (WMF)
items.attribution: "Editing basics - watchlists" by Sage Ross (WMF), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: A narrated Wikipedia tutorial: page changes, menus and small interface text at 1280x1024. Human English captions exist on Commons (47 cues; the last cue's end is written 99:59:59, a useful sidecar case). Shows the narrator's own Wikipedia account and public user names.

items.title: Structured Data on Commons uploads by the Metropolitan Museum of Art 01
items.author: GFontenelle (WMF); workshop by Jennie Choi, the Metropolitan Museum of Art
items.attribution: "Structured Data on Commons uploads by the Metropolitan Museum of Art 01" by GFontenelle (WMF), CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: A live tool demonstration in a recorded office-hours call (PetScan, QuickStatements): speech with pauses while the presenter works, screen changes, about 31 chunks. Other call participants may be visible in tiles: to be checked before approval.

items.title: After the lifting of the block: Case study of Turkey (Wikimania 2021)
items.author: Basak, Khutuck (Wikimania 2021; credit WMF)
items.attribution: "After the lifting of the block: Case study of Turkey" by Basak and Khutuck, Wikimania 2021, CC BY-SA 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: A pre-recorded 19-minute conference talk by two speakers in Turkish-accented English, about 46 chunks. It opens with music and a title card: its captions put music from 8.2 s and the first words at 13.4 s, so the lead is non-speech rather than silence (to be labelled by listening). Its English captions look machine-made, so they are no reference transcript. A 480p transcode (29,909,095 bytes, no published checksum) is the lighter alternative.

items.title: Como contribuir com o Structured Data on Commons
items.author: Ederporto
items.attribution: "Como contribuir com o Structured Data on Commons" by Ederporto, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: A Brazilian Portuguese tutorial with interface changes. Commons has Brazilian Portuguese captions (46 cues), a possible reference transcript. The audio track is tagged English in its metadata, which is wrong (a language-detection case).

items.title: President Reagan's Trip to Fullerton and San Bernardino on November 1, 1988
items.author: Reagan Library (White House Television Office)
items.attribution: "President Reagan's Trip to Fullerton and San Bernardino on November 1, 1988" by the Reagan Library, CC BY 3.0, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: Archival White House television footage: remarks at a campaign rally in a gymnasium (crowd noise) and at a helicopter landing zone (field microphone), between arrival shots; old analogue video. Its licence was reviewed on Commons. The noise is described by its source, not yet heard.

items.title: Space Station Astronaut Discusses Record Breaking Mission with Previous Record Holder
items.author: NASA Johnson Space Center
items.attribution: "Space Station Astronaut Discusses Record Breaking Mission with Previous Record Holder" by NASA Johnson Space Center, public domain, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: A conversation between an astronaut on the station and a former record holder in Mission Control (NASA employees in their role): two voices, turn-taking and the pauses of a space-to-ground link, about 25 chunks. NASA media carries no endorsement and NASA's logos keep their own rules; the set uses the recording for testing only.

items.title: Introduction to Wikidata Lexeme Forms - Lucas Werkmeister - Lexicodays 2024 (480p transcode)
items.author: Lucas Werkmeister
items.attribution: "Introduction to Wikidata Lexeme Forms - Lucas Werkmeister - Lexicodays 2024" by Lucas Werkmeister, CC BY-SA 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons (480p transcode)

media.video: VP9 854x480 (Commons transcode of a VP8 1920x1080 25 fps original)

items.notes: One speaker in German-accented English demonstrating a web tool, about 23 chunks. Commons has human-made English captions (205 cues), the best reference transcript of the set. The original is 254,967,178 bytes, so the 480p transcode is proposed; Commons publishes no checksum for transcodes, so source_checksum is the object store's ETag taken as the MD5 (unconfirmed until the pin) and the pin is otherwise trust on first use.

items.title: Mark Carney speaking about climate action and energy security in Calgary, 15 May 2026
items.author: Jasonhargrove
items.attribution: "Mark Carney speaking about climate action and energy security in Calgary, 15 May 2026" by Jasonhargrove, CC BY 4.0, via Wikimedia Commons
items.notes: Optional. A vertical phone recording of a public speech in a hall, re-encoded to WebM before upload, so its frame rate may no longer vary. The file page carries a transcript and a personality-rights warning (the likeness of a public figure; testing is not a commercial use). A current politician: the maintainer may prefer to leave it out.
